chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: The 'about' property directly matches the meaning of 'has subject' for events and their topics.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: actor
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actor is 'Tom Hanks'.", "A play's actor is 'The Ensemble Theatre'.", "An episode's actor is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: mainContentOfPage
candidates.comment: A main content relation between a web page and the web page element that constitutes its primary subject. Also called: primary content, central element, core content. Examples: "Article Page mainContentOfPage ArticleBody", "Product Page mainContentOfPage ProductDescription", "Blog Post mainContentOfPage PostContent".

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

relations.definition: Indicates that a subject is the initial instance of an action or status within a specified group or category.

candidates.label: actionStatus
candidates.comment: An action status relation between an action and its current disposition or state. Also called action state, status of action, disposition. Examples: "A 'purchase' action's action status is 'CompletedActionStatus'.", "A 'shipment' action's action status is 'PotentialActionStatus'."

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: beforeMedia
candidates.comment: A media object representing the circumstances prior to performing a how-to direction. Also called: pre-action media, initial state media. Examples: "HowToDirection 'Install Shelf' beforeMedia 'Image of empty wall'", "HowToDirection 'Bake Cake' beforeMedia 'Video of ingredients on counter'."

candidates.label: status
candidates.comment: An indication of the current state or status of a medical condition, procedure, or study. Also called "current state", "condition status", "study progress", "procedure status". Examples: "The medical study has status Recruiting", "The patient's condition status is stable", "The procedure's status is completed."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: certificationStatus
candidates.comment: A status relation for a certification, indicating whether it is active or inactive. Also called "certificate status", "certification validity", "status of certification". Examples: "Product certification certificationStatus Active", "Company certification certificationStatus Inactive".

candidates.label: pageStart
candidates.comment: The page number or identifier where a work (article, chapter, etc.) begins. Also called starting page, first page, initial page number. Examples: "Article X pageStart 135", "Chapter Y pageStart 'xiii'", "Report Z pageStart 1". Distinct from pageEnd, which is the concluding page. pagination is a general range.

candidates.label: collection

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: afterMedia
candidates.comment: An after media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL depicting the state or circumstances after completing that step. Also called post-step media, result image, outcome visual. Examples: "A recipe direction's after media is an image of the mixed ingredients.", "The assembly instruction's after media is a video of the connected parts."

candidates.label: equal
candidates.comment: An equality relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject qualitative value is considered equal to the object qualitative value within a specific ordering context. Also called "is equivalent to", "is the same as", "matches". Examples: "Qualitative value 'Satisfactory' equal 'Acceptable'", "Qualitative value 'Medium' equal 'Average'", "Qualitative value 'High' equal 'Very Good'".

candidates.label: resultReview

Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: causeOf

Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome

candidates.label: produces

candidates.label: mentions

Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Also called: guideline topic, subject matter, focus. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" guideline subject "Hypertension", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" guideline subject "Type 2 Diabetes", "WHO COVID-19 Guidelines" guideline subject "COVID-19". Distinct from guideline, which is the guideline itself.

candidates.label: mainEntity

Examples: "A job posting for 'Software Engineer' has a relevant occupation 'Software Developer'.", "A job posting for 'Nurse Practitioner' has a relevant occupation 'Registered Nurse'.", "A job posting for 'Marketing Manager' has a relevant occupation 'Marketing Professional'."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: jurisdiction
candidates.comment: A legal scope relation between a government service or legislation and the administrative area or territory where it applies. Also called legal authority, governing area, applicable region, domain of law. Examples: A government service has a jurisdiction of 'California'. Legislation has a jurisdiction of 'United States federal law'. A permit applies to the jurisdiction of 'City of London'. Distinct from eligibleRegion or ineligibleRegion, which are about availability, not legal authority.

candidates.label: relatedCondition
candidates.comment: A related condition relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical condition associated with it. Also called associated condition, condition of, affects condition. Examples: "The knee joint has a related condition 'arthritis'.", "The respiratory system has a related condition 'asthma'.", "The skin has a related condition 'eczema'."

candidates.label: applicableLocation

Also called valid location, jurisdiction, region of applicability. Examples: "A drug's legal status's applicable location is 'California'.", "The drug cost's applicable location is 'Europe'."

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: announcementLocation

Also called relevant location, associated place, specific venue. Examples: "A special announcement's announcement location is 'City Hall'.", "The emergency announcement's announcement location is 'Local Grocery Store'." Distinct from spatialCoverage, which is used for larger geographic regions.

candidates.label: appliesToDeliveryMethod

Also called delivery method scope, applicable shipping method. Examples: "A delivery charge specification applies to 'ShippingMethod.Express'.", "The payment charge specification applies to 'DeliveryMethod.Pickup'."

candidates.label: appliesToPaymentMethod
candidates.comment: An applies to payment method relation between a payment charge specification and the payment method(s) to which it is relevant. Also called payment method scope, applicable payment type. Examples: "A payment charge specification applies to 'PaymentMethod.CreditCard'.", "The charge applies to 'PaymentMethod.PayPal'."

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: equal

candidates.label: subjectOf

candidates.label: representativeOfPage

candidates.label: object

Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: encoding

candidates.label: isPartOf

Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: sameAs

Examples: `Person: Albert Einstein` sameAs `Wikipedia URL`, `Organization: Google` sameAs `Official Website URL`, `Product: iPhone` sameAs `Wikidata URL`. candidates.label: hasDigitalDocumentPermission

Examples: "A digital document has a digital document permission to read.", "The file has a digital document permission for editing.", "This document has digital document permissions for public viewing."

candidates.label: serviceUrl
candidates.comment: The URL of the website used to access a service. Also called service website, online service portal, service access URL. Examples: `Online Banking Channel` serviceUrl `URL: bank.com/online`, `Government Portal` serviceUrl `URL: gov.agency/services`, `E-commerce Service` serviceUrl `URL: shop.com/support`. Distinct from `url`, which is a general URL for an entity.

candidates.label: serviceSmsNumber

Examples: `Customer Support Channel` serviceSmsNumber `ContactPoint: 555-TEXT-HELP`, `Alert Service` serviceSmsNumber `ContactPoint: 222-ALERTS`, `Booking Service` serviceSmsNumber `ContactPoint: 444-BOOK`. candidates.label: safetyConsideration
candidates.comment: Any potential safety concerns, interactions, or adverse reactions associated with a dietary supplement. Also called supplement warnings, safety warnings, adverse effects. Examples: `St. John's Wort` safetyConsideration `"May interact with antidepressants"`, `Creatine Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Not recommended for individuals with kidney issues"`, `Vitamin D Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Avoid excessive dosage"`.

candidates.label: contraindication
candidates.comment: A medical restriction relation for a medical device or therapy, indicating a contraindication. Also called "medical warning", "precaution", "not recommended for". Examples: "Drug therapy contraindication 'Pregnancy'", "Medical device contraindication 'Pacemaker users'".

candidates.label: warning
candidates.comment: A warning relation between a drug and any FDA or other safety advisories. Also called drug warning, safety advisory, health alert. Examples: "Drug warning 'May cause drowsiness.'", "Drug warning 'https://fda.gov/drug-warnings/xyz'", "Medication warning 'Do not exceed recommended dose.'".

candidates.label: pregnancyWarning
candidates.comment: A medical attribute providing precautions, guidance, or contraindications regarding a drug's use during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy precautions, drug-pregnancy risks, maternal warnings. Examples: A drug has a pregnancy warning 'Consult doctor before use'. The medication includes a pregnancy warning about 'potential fetal harm'. There is a pregnancy warning against 'use in first trimester'.

candidates.label: accessibilityHazard
candidates.comment: An accessibility hazard relation between a creative work and a characteristic that poses a physiological danger to some users. Also called accessibility risk, dangerous feature, user hazard. Examples: "A video's accessibility hazard is 'flashingLights'.", "A game's accessibility hazard is 'motionSimulation'."

candidates.label: pregnancyCategory
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating the pregnancy category assigned to a drug. Also called drug safety in pregnancy, pregnancy risk classification. Examples: A drug has a pregnancy category of 'Category C'. The medication is assigned pregnancy category 'B'. This drug falls under pregnancy category 'X'.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: lesser
candidates.comment: A lesser ordering relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject value is smaller than the object value. Also called: is less than, is smaller than, falls below. Examples: "Low lesser Medium", "Small lesser Large", "Cold lesser Warm". Distinct from lesserOrEqual, which includes equality.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: legislationCommences
candidates.comment: A legislative activation relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it brings into legal effect. Also called brings into force, enacts, activates law, sets into effect. Examples: Legislation A legislationCommences 'Legislation B'. The enabling act legislationCommences 'the new regulations'. This decree legislationCommences 'the policy changes'.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: educationalUse
candidates.comment: An educational use relation between a creative work or learning resource and its purpose in an educational context. Also called "learning purpose", "pedagogical use", "instructional application". Examples: "Worksheet educationalUse 'Assignment'", "Video educationalUse 'Group work'", "Simulation educationalUse 'Experiment'".

candidates.label: legislationApplies
candidates.comment: An informative legislative transfer relation indicating that a piece of legislation incorporates or references another legislation within a different legal context, without legal binding. Also called incorporates legislation, references law, applies provisions of, draws from legislation. Examples: A national law legislationApplies 'a European Directive'. A local ordinance legislationApplies 'state regulations'. This consolidated law legislationApplies 'the original act'. Distinct from legislationTransposes, which implies a legally binding transposition.

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: collection
candidates.comment: A target relation for an update action, indicating the collection that is being updated. Also called "target collection", "updated collection", "collection object". Examples: "Add item update action collection 'Shopping Cart'", "Remove item update action collection 'Wishlist'".

Examples: "Athlete Role namedPosition 'Quarterback'", "Employee Role namedPosition 'Senior Software Engineer'", "Board Member Role namedPosition 'Treasurer'". candidates.label: jobTitle

Examples: A person has a jobTitle of 'Software Engineer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Chief Executive Officer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Marketing Manager'.

candidates.label: roleName
candidates.comment: The specific designation or title of a role performed by a person or organization. Also called role title, position name, function name. Examples: `Person in Movie` roleName `"Actor"`, `Team Member` roleName `"Quarterback"`, `Project Contributor` roleName `"Lead Developer"`.

candidates.label: title
candidates.comment: A title relation between a job posting and the descriptive name of the job. Also called job name, position title, role title. Examples: "Job posting title 'Software Engineer'", "Job posting title 'Marketing Manager'", "Job posting title 'Data Scientist'".

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. candidates.label: hiringOrganization

Examples: "A job posting has a hiring organization 'Acme Corp'.", "The position is offered by a hiring organization.", "This job posting lists the hiring organization."

candidates.label: employee

candidates.label: legalName

Examples: An organization has a legalName of 'Acme Corporation Inc.'. A company's legalName is 'Global Solutions LLC'. The charity's legalName is 'Helping Hands Foundation'. Distinct from name, which is the common or display name.

candidates.label: numberedPosition

Examples: "Athlete Role numberedPosition 23", "Team Member Role numberedPosition 7", "Employee Role numberedPosition 101". Distinct from namedPosition, which is a textual name for a role.

candidates.label: employees
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and the people who work for it. Also called "staff", "workforce", "personnel". Examples: "How-to direction 'Attach part A' duringMedia 'Video of assembly'", "Direction 'Stir mixture' duringMedia 'Image of stirring technique'".

candidates.label: buyer

candidates.label: caption

candidates.label: collection

candidates.label: contentLocation

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". candidates.label: locationCreated

Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: address
candidates.comment: An address relation between an entity (e.g., organization, person, place) and its physical postal address. Also called physical location, mailing address, street address. Examples: "A company's address is '123 Main St, Anytown'.", "A person's address is 'PO Box 123'.", "The restaurant's address is '456 Oak Ave'."

candidates.label: geoWithin
candidates.comment: A geo within relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is located entirely inside the interior of another containing geometry or place. Also called: is inside, contained in, located within. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo within "Country 'France'", "Office 'Suite 100'" geo within "Building 'Empire State'", "State 'California'" geo within "Country 'USA'". Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: arrivalTerminal
candidates.comment: A terminal identifier for a flight's arrival location. Also called: flight destination terminal, terminal of arrival. Examples: "Flight BA286 arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 5'", "Flight from Tokyo arrivalTerminal 'North Terminal'", "Flight to JFK arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 4'". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is for train trips.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: expectedArrivalUntil
candidates.comment: An expected arrival until relation between a parcel delivery and the latest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: latest arrival, maximum delivery date, estimated end arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival until "2023-10-28", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival until "2023-10-27T17:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival until "2023-11-05". Distinct from expectedArrivalFrom, which is the earliest arrival date.

candidates.label: itemReviewed

Also called reviewed item, rated item, subject of review, evaluated entity. Examples: A review has an itemReviewed of 'Restaurant X'. An aggregate rating has an itemReviewed of 'Movie Y'. A product review has an itemReviewed of 'Smartphone Z'. Distinct from itemOffered, which is the subject of an offer or demand.

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: reviewCount
candidates.comment: The total number of individual reviews contributing to an aggregate rating. Also called total reviews, number of reviews, review tally. Examples: `Product Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `150`, `Movie Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `5000`, `Service Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `75`.

candidates.label: question
candidates.comment: A question relation between an ask action and the specific question being posed. Also called asked question, inquiry. Examples: "An ask action involves the question 'What is the capital of France?'.", "A survey asks the question 'How satisfied are you with our service?'.", "A forum post poses the question 'How do I fix this error?'."

candidates.label: commentCount
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement for a creative work, indicating the total number of comments it has received. Also called "number of comments", "comment total", "feedback count". Examples: "Blog post commentCount 15", "Article commentCount 200".

candidates.label: measuredProperty
candidates.comment: A measured property relation between an observation or statistical variable and the property being measured. Also called: property measured, observed characteristic, variable property. Examples: "Temperature Observation measuredProperty 'temperature'", "GDP StatisticalVariable measuredProperty 'Gross Domestic Product'", "Survey Response measuredProperty 'satisfaction level'". Distinct from variableMeasured, which is a broader property for describing what is measured in a dataset.

candidates.label: reviewedBy
candidates.comment: The person or organization responsible for reviewing the content of a webpage for accuracy or completeness. Also called content reviewer, page editor, accuracy checker. Examples: `Medical Information Page` reviewedBy `Dr. Jane Doe`, `News Article` reviewedBy `Fact-Checking Organization`, `Research Paper` reviewedBy `Peer Review Board`. Distinct from `author`, which indicates who created the content, not who reviewed it.

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: claimInterpreter

candidates.label: claimReviewed

candidates.label: status

candidates.label: itemCondition
candidates.comment: A product state relation indicating the physical condition of a product or service, or the condition required for returns. Also called product state, condition of item, quality status, return condition. Examples: An offer has an itemCondition of 'NewCondition'. A product has an itemCondition of 'UsedCondition'. A return policy specifies itemCondition 'SellerRefurbished'.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. candidates.label: associatedClaimReview

candidates.label: verificationFactCheckingPolicy

candidates.label: object

candidates.label: remainingAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A remaining attendee capacity relation between an event and the number of available spots for attendees. Also called available seats, remaining tickets, open spots. Examples: "A concert has a remaining attendee capacity of 100.", "A workshop has a remaining attendee capacity of 5.", "A conference has a remaining attendee capacity of 500."

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: endTime
candidates.comment: An end time relation between an item (such as an action, reservation, or media object) and the time it is expected to conclude or when a clip ends. Also called "conclusion time", "finish time", "closing time". Examples: "Reservation 'Dinner' endTime '20:00'", "Action 'Meeting' endTime '17:00'", "Media clip endTime '00:02:30'". Distinct from endDate, which specifies the end date for longer-term items like events or seasons.

candidates.label: collection
candidates.comment: A target relation for an update action, indicating the collection that is being updated. Also called "target collection", "updated collection", "collection object". Examples: "Add item update action collection 'Shopping Cart'", "Remove item update action collection 'Wishlist'".

candidates.label: workPerformed
candidates.comment: A performed work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is enacted or presented live during the event. Also called enacted work, live presentation, staged work. Examples: TheaterEvent workPerformed "Hamlet", ConcertEvent workPerformed "Symphony No. 5", DancePerformance workPerformed "Swan Lake". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPresented, which is specifically for movies at screening events.

candidates.label: countriesNotSupported

candidates.label: ineligibleRegion

Also called restricted region, excluded region, unavailable in, not valid in. Examples: An offer has an ineligibleRegion of 'Alaska'. A delivery charge specification has an ineligibleRegion of 'Hawaii'. A media object has an ineligibleRegion of 'EU'. Distinct from eligibleRegion, which specifies where something *is* valid or available.

candidates.label: dateDeleted

Examples: "Expired Job Posting" date deleted "2023-06-30", "Outdated Product Listing" date deleted "2023-01-01T00:00:00Z".

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy

Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy
candidates.comment: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

candidates.label: contraindication
candidates.comment: A medical restriction relation for a medical device or therapy, indicating a contraindication. Also called "medical warning", "precaution", "not recommended for". Examples: "Drug therapy contraindication 'Pregnancy'", "Medical device contraindication 'Pacemaker users'".

candidates.label: legislationRepeals
candidates.comment: A repeal relation between two pieces of legislation, where one cancels or abrogates the other. Also called: cancels, abrogates, revokes. Examples: "New Act legislationRepeals Old Act", "Regulation X legislationRepeals Directive Y", "Law 123 legislationRepeals Statute 456".

candidates.label: bccRecipient

candidates.label: hasPart

candidates.label: includedComposition

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart

candidates.label: includedInDataCatalog

candidates.label: includedDataCatalog

candidates.label: isPartOf

Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: comprisedOf

candidates.label: geoContains

Examples: "Country 'France'" geo contains "City 'Paris'", "Continent 'Europe'" geo contains "Country 'Germany'", "Building 'Empire State'" geo contains "Office 'Suite 100'". Distinct from geoWithin, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: review
candidates.comment: A critical assessment or evaluation of an item, such as a product, service, or creative work. Also called item review, evaluation, critique, assessment. Examples: `Product: Smartphone` review `Customer Review`, `Movie: Inception` review `Film Critic's Review`, `Restaurant: The Fancy Bistro` review `Food Blogger's Review`. Distinct from `reviews`, which is a plural form and often implies a collection.

candidates.label: payload
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the maximum permitted weight of passengers and cargo a vehicle can carry, excluding the vehicle's own weight. Also called carrying capacity, load capacity, cargo weight limit. Examples: A truck has a payload of 1000 kg. A car has a payload of 500 kg. An aircraft has a payload of 20,000 lbs. Distinct from weight, which refers to the weight of the empty vehicle itself.

candidates.label: contentSize
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement for a media object, indicating its file size. Also called "file size", "media size", "data size". Examples: "Image file contentSize '2.5MB'", "Video file contentSize '500MB'".

relations.definition: Indicates the action of limiting or controlling the object.
relations.embedding_query_text: to restrict: Indicates the action of limiting or controlling the object.

instances: landmark legislation -> children's access to social media

chosen_property.label: aimsToRestrict
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that the subject has the purpose of limiting or controlling the object.
chosen_property.justification: No suitable schema.org property found for legislation aiming to restrict a permit.

candidates.label: requiresSubscription
candidates.comment: A subscription requirement relation indicating whether an action access or media object necessitates a subscription for use. Also called subscription needed, paywall, access restriction. Examples: "A streaming movie requires subscription 'true'.", "A news article requires subscription 'false'.", "A premium feature requires subscription 'true'."

candidates.label: constraintProperty
candidates.comment: A definitional relation for a constraint node, indicating a property used as a constraint. Also called "constraining property", "restricted by property", "property constraint". Examples: "Statistical variable constraint node constraintProperty 'schema:age'", "Data filter constraintProperty 'dc:gender'".

candidates.label: contraindication
candidates.comment: A medical restriction relation for a medical device or therapy, indicating a contraindication. Also called "medical warning", "precaution", "not recommended for". Examples: "Drug therapy contraindication 'Pregnancy'", "Medical device contraindication 'Pacemaker users'".

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: numConstraints
candidates.comment: The number of constraint property values defined for a constraint node. Also called constraint count, number of restrictions, defined constraints. Examples: "Statistical Variable A numConstraints 3", "Data Filter B numConstraints 2", "Query Parameter C numConstraints 1".

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: suitableForDiet
candidates.comment: An indication of a dietary restriction or guideline for which a recipe or menu item is appropriate. Also called "dietary suitability", "dietary compliance", "dietary restriction friendly", "accommodates diet". Examples: "The recipe is suitableForDiet VeganDiet", "The menu item's suitableForDiet is GlutenFreeDiet", "This dish is suitableForDiet HalalDiet."

candidates.label: travelBans
candidates.comment: A travel bans relation between a special announcement and information regarding restrictions on travel. Also called travel restrictions, ban on travel, travel advisories. Examples: "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'https://example.com/travel-restrictions'", "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'All international travel is suspended.'", "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'https://who.int/travel-guidance'".

candidates.label: collection
candidates.comment: A target relation for an update action, indicating the collection that is being updated. Also called "target collection", "updated collection", "collection object". Examples: "Add item update action collection 'Shopping Cart'", "Remove item update action collection 'Wishlist'".

candidates.label: numItems
candidates.comment: A limit on the number of items being shipped for which specific shipping conditions apply. Also called item quantity limit, shipping item count, maximum items. Examples: "Free Shipping Conditions numItems 'max 5'", "Bulk Discount Shipping numItems 'min 10'", "Special Rate Shipping numItems '1-3'". Distinct from orderQuantity, which is the quantity of a specific item in an order.

relations.definition: Indicates that the subject has the potential to offer or supply the object.
relations.embedding_query_text: may provide: Indicates that the subject has the potential to offer or supply the object.

instances: France may provide an early test case -> early test case

chosen_property.label: mayProvide
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that the subject has the potential to offer or supply the object.
chosen_property.justification: No suitable schema.org property found for a policy role prediction potentially providing a precedent.

candidates.label: itemOffered
candidates.comment: A transaction subject relation between a demand or offer and the specific item, product, service, or event being requested or provided. Also called offered item, demanded item, subject of offer, product/service offered. Examples: An offer has an itemOffered of 'a new car'. A demand has an itemOffered of 'web design service'. An offer has an itemOffered of 'a concert ticket'. Distinct from itemReviewed, which is the subject of a review, not an offer/demand.

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: provider
candidates.comment: A provision relation between an action, work, program, or service and the organization or person that supplies or performs it. Also called supplied by, performed by, offered by, produced by. Examples: "A parcel delivery is provided by FedEx.", "A financial incentive is provided by the government.", "A medical service is provided by Dr. Smith."

candidates.label: makesOffer
candidates.comment: An offering relation between an organization or person and the offer for products or services they provide. Also called: offers, provides, sells. Examples: "Retailer makesOffer Discounted Electronics", "Consultant makesOffer Business Strategy Services", "Restaurant makesOffer Dinner Menu".

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: seeks
candidates.comment: A demand for specific products or services expressed by an organization or person. Also called desires, looks for, requests, requires. Examples: `Company X` seeks `Demand for Software Developers`, `Person Y` seeks `Demand for Used Car`, `Organization Z` seeks `Demand for Consulting Services`. Distinct from `offers`, which is about what is provided.

candidates.label: buyer
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sell action, indicating the organization or person who purchased the object. Also called "purchaser", "customer", "acquired by". Examples: "Online purchase sell action buyer Jane Doe", "Company acquisition sell action buyer Acme Corp". Distinct from seller, which is the party offering the object for sale.

candidates.label: offers
candidates.comment: An offer or demand related to a product, service, event, or other item. Also called available offers, related offers, product offers. Examples: "Product X offers 'Offer to sell'", "Service Y offers 'Demand for service'", "Event Z offers 'Offer for tickets'". Distinct from hasOfferCatalog, which points to a catalog of offers.

candidates.label: includesObject
candidates.comment: A composition relation between an offer or product collection and the specific products and their quantities it contains. Also called composed of, contains, comprises, consists of, has as object. Examples: An offer includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 2 apples. A product collection includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 5 books. A demand includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 1 car.

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
candidates.comment: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only. Examples: "An offer has adult consideration for explicit content.", "A product is tagged with adult consideration.", "This item has adult consideration due to its theme."

relations.definition: Indicates that the subject is observing or monitoring the object.
relations.embedding_query_text: are watching: Indicates that the subject is observing or monitoring the object.

instances: Governments -> France bans social media for children

chosen_property.label: observes
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that the subject is observing or monitoring the object.
chosen_property.justification: No suitable schema.org property found for an organization observing an event.

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: observationPeriod
candidates.comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: timeRequired
candidates.comment: A duration representing the approximate time typically needed for an audience to engage with or complete a creative work. Also called "completion time", "estimated duration", "reading time", "viewing time". Examples: "The article has timeRequired 10 minutes", "The course's timeRequired is 40 hours", "This creative work takes timeRequired 2 hours to watch."

candidates.label: variableMeasured
candidates.comment: A variable measured relation between a dataset or observation and the variables that are measured within it. Also called measured variable, data variable, observation parameter. Examples: "Dataset variableMeasured 'Temperature'", "Observation variableMeasured 'Humidity'", "Dataset variableMeasured 'Patient Age'".

candidates.label: colorSwatch
candidates.comment: A visual representation for a product, providing an image object or URL of its color swatch. Also called "color image", "color sample", "swatch URL". Examples: "Product 'T-shirt' colorSwatch 'https://example.com/red-swatch.jpg'", "Product 'Paint' colorSwatch ImageObject". Distinct from color, which is the textual description of the color.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: isLiveBroadcast
candidates.comment: A broadcast status relation indicating whether a broadcast event is being transmitted in real-time. Also called live stream, real-time broadcast, live transmission. Examples: A sports game broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A news report broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A recorded TV show broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'false'.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: itemReviewed
candidates.comment: A review subject relation between an aggregate rating or review and the entity that is being evaluated or rated. Also called reviewed item, rated item, subject of review, evaluated entity. Examples: A review has an itemReviewed of 'Restaurant X'. An aggregate rating has an itemReviewed of 'Movie Y'. A product review has an itemReviewed of 'Smartphone Z'. Distinct from itemOffered, which is the subject of an offer or demand.

relations.definition: Indicates the purpose of observing, which is to determine if the subject successfully reaches the object.
relations.embedding_query_text: to see if achieves: Indicates the purpose of observing, which is to determine if the subject successfully reaches the object.

instances: France bans social media for children -> intended aims

chosen_property.label: assesses
chosen_property.justification: The 'assesses' property captures the meaning of evaluating if the SocialMediaBanEvent achieves its Goal.

Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: measurementQualifier
candidates.comment: A measurement qualifier relation between an observation or statistical variable and an enumeration providing additional qualification. Also called: observation qualifier, measurement attribute, data context. Examples: "GDP Observation measurementQualifier 'Nominal'", "Inflation Rate measurementQualifier 'Annualized'", "Population Count measurementQualifier 'Estimated'".

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: measuredProperty
candidates.comment: A measured property relation between an observation or statistical variable and the property being measured. Also called: property measured, observed characteristic, variable property. Examples: "Temperature Observation measuredProperty 'temperature'", "GDP StatisticalVariable measuredProperty 'Gross Domestic Product'", "Survey Response measuredProperty 'satisfaction level'". Distinct from variableMeasured, which is a broader property for describing what is measured in a dataset.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: assesses
candidates.comment: A relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is intended to evaluate. Also called: evaluates, measures, tests, gauges. Examples: "LearningResource 'Quiz' assesses 'Understanding of Algebra'", "EducationEvent 'Exam' assesses 'Problem-solving skills'", "CreativeWork 'Rubric' assesses 'Writing proficiency'."

candidates.label: variableMeasured
candidates.comment: A variable measured relation between a dataset or observation and the variables that are measured within it. Also called measured variable, data variable, observation parameter. Examples: "Dataset variableMeasured 'Temperature'", "Observation variableMeasured 'Humidity'", "Dataset variableMeasured 'Patient Age'".

relations.embedding_query_text: is first country in:

instances: France -> European Union

chosen_property.label: isFirstMemberOf
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that the subject is the initial country or member in a specified consortium or group.
chosen_property.justification: No suitable schema.org property found for a country being the first member of a consortium.

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: countryOfAssembly
candidates.comment: A manufacturing location relation between a product and the country where it was assembled. Also called: assembled in, manufacturing country, assembly location. Examples: "Smartphone" country of assembly "China", "Car" country of assembly "Mexico", "Laptop" country of assembly "Vietnam". Distinct from countryOfOrigin, which refers to the country of the principal offices or where the product originates.

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: dateVehicleFirstRegistered
candidates.comment: A temporal registration relation between a vehicle and the date of its first registration with public authorities. Also called: first registration date, initial registration, vehicle registration date. Examples: "Car" date vehicle first registered "2018-03-15", "Motorcycle" date vehicle first registered "2020-07-01", "Truck" date vehicle first registered "2015-11-20".

candidates.label: nationality
candidates.comment: A country representing the nationality of a person. Also called citizenship, country of origin, national identity. Examples: "Person A nationality 'United States'", "Person B nationality 'France'", "Person C nationality 'Japan'". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the location where a person was born.

candidates.label: addressCountry
candidates.comment: An address country relation between a defined region, geo-coordinates, geo-shape, or postal address and the country it is located within. Also called nation, country code, geographic country. Examples: "A postal address's address country is 'US'.", "The coordinates' address country is 'France'."

candidates.label: countriesSupported
candidates.comment: A geographical availability relation between a software application and the countries where it is supported. Also called: supported regions, available in, operational in. Examples: "App X" countries supported "USA, Canada", "Software Y" countries supported "Germany, France, UK", "Game Z" countries supported "Japan, South Korea". Distinct from countriesNotSupported, which lists where the application is not supported.

candidates.label: copyrightYear
candidates.comment: A temporal relation between a creative work and the year its copyright was first asserted. Also called: year of copyright, copyright date, first copyright year. Examples: "Classic Album" copyright year "1970", "Software Version 1.0" copyright year "2005", "Research Paper" copyright year "2022". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first publication or broadcast.

candidates.label: countryOfLastProcessing
candidates.comment: A final processing location relation between a product and the country where it underwent its last processing and testing before importation. Also called: last processed in, final testing country, pre-importation processing location. Examples: "Electronic Component" country of last processing "Malaysia", "Textile Product" country of last processing "Bangladesh", "Automotive Part" country of last processing "Thailand". Distinct from countryOfOrigin, which is about the origin of the product itself.
